questions.stem: What is the difference between an ischaemic stroke and a haemorrhagic stroke?

options.text: An ischaemic stroke is caused by a blocked blood vessel; a haemorrhagic stroke is caused by a burst blood vessel
An ischaemic stroke affects the heart; a haemorrhagic stroke affects the brain
An ischaemic stroke is minor; a haemorrhagic stroke is always fatal
An ischaemic stroke is caused by high cholesterol; a haemorrhagic stroke is caused by smoking

questions.explanation: An ischaemic stroke (about 85% of strokes) occurs when a blood clot blocks a vessel in the brain. A haemorrhagic stroke (about 15%) occurs when a blood vessel in the brain bursts, causing bleeding.
